samples.question: This image shows four framed square panels of identical size standing side by side in one row, numbered 1 to 4 from left to right. Every panel is ruled with the same faint square lattice of cells, and every panel holds exactly five solid dots of the same single colour and the same size, each dot sitting in the middle of its own lattice cell, so all four panels carry the same number of dots and the same amount of ink and no two dots ever share a cell. A pair of dots counts as aligned when the two dots sit in the same lattice row, so that they stand at the same height as each other, or in the same lattice column, so that they stand directly one above the other. Exactly one panel is clear: no two of its five dots are aligned, so its dots occupy five different lattice rows and five different lattice columns. Each of the other three panels contains exactly one aligned pair, either two dots sharing a row or two dots sharing a column, which leaves one of its rows or columns doubled and another one empty. Which lattice cells the dots occupy, how many lattice cells a panel is ruled into, where the dots sit inside a panel, and whether an aligned pair shares a row or a column are all arbitrary and carry no information. The lattice is drawn but no alignment is marked in the image, and the judgement must be made from the drawn dot positions alone. Does the clear panel, the one with no two dots aligned in a row or in a column, lie in the left half of the row of panels (panels 1 and 2) or in the right half (panels 3 and 4)? Answer with exactly one of: left, right.
